purpose: Evaluate retrieval relevance and traceability on a new published transit-network paper without DeepSeek calls. Single-reviewer initial labels require second adjudication before science-quality inference.

heldout_source.title: Quantifying temporal vulnerability of urban multi-modal transit networks under interdependent cascading failures
heldout_source.source_summary_for_domain_context: Urban multi-modal transit network vulnerability; subway and bus passenger flow redistribution, station capacity, and coupled cascading failures after disruption.

label_definitions.direct_near: Domain-matched original research directly studies transit-network disruption, flow redistribution, operational resilience or capacity effects; not automatically a verified novelty-killing paper.
label_definitions.domain_context: Same transportation field but review/background instead of directly tested competing mechanism.
label_definitions.method_transfer: Potentially transferable analytical method from a different field; requires explicit input/output bridge and human review before use.
label_definitions.unrelated: Not an evidenced urban transport scientific neighbor; should be quarantined from direct-prior claims.
label_definitions.source_self: Held-out source itself; never an independent prior work.

evaluation_limits.input_policy: Publisher-verified DOI and title only. The live benchmark reconstructs real OpenAlex abstracts in memory; report stores hashes, metadata and aggregate metrics, not raw abstracts or PDFs.

items.title: Urban rail transit resilience under different operation schemes: A percolation-based approach
items.label: direct_near
items.reviewer_rationale: Rail percolation, operation schemes and resilience thresholds explicitly overlap the held-out paper's transit capacity/cascade mechanism.

items.title: Resilience assessment of an urban rail transit network under natural disasters
items.label: direct_near
items.reviewer_rationale: Train-schedule-based rail resilience under disaster disruptions is a substantive adjacent transit mechanism.

items.title: Assessing flood resilience of urban rail transit systems: Complex network modelling and stress testing in a case study of London
items.label: direct_near
items.reviewer_rationale: Dynamic rail service loss under floods and recovery modelling directly relates to transit disruption and network resilience.

items.title: Urban rail transit disruption management: Research progress and future directions
items.label: domain_context
items.reviewer_rationale: Sector review supplies background on disruption management but is not by itself a directly tested competing mechanism.

items.title: Assessing transport network resilience: empirical insights from real-world data studies
items.label: domain_context
items.reviewer_rationale: Empirical transport resilience review; relevant context, not a direct mechanism-specific nearest experiment.

items.title: A small set of critical hyper-motifs governs heterogeneous flow-weighted network resilience
items.label: method_transfer
items.reviewer_rationale: General flow-weighted network motifs may transfer as a method, but application to this transit system is unverified.

items.title: Dimension reduction approach for understanding resource-flow resilience to climate change
items.label: method_transfer
items.reviewer_rationale: Low-dimensional infrastructure-flow framework could inspire method transfer, not direct transit precedent.

items.title: Measuring system resilience through a comparison of information- and flow-based network analyses
items.label: method_transfer
items.reviewer_rationale: Information/flow network comparison may be transferable after cross-domain assumptions are examined.

items.title: The connectivity indices concept of neutrosophic graph and their application of computer network, highway system and transport network flow
items.label: method_transfer
items.reviewer_rationale: Abstract mathematical connectivity indices include transport examples; no verified metro capacity/cascading mechanism.

items.title: Network-based restoration strategies maximize ecosystem recovery
items.label: method_transfer
items.reviewer_rationale: Ecological recovery prioritization could be a cross-domain intervention analogy, not rail prior work.

items.title: Network-driven anomalous transport is a fundamental component of brain microvascular dysfunction
items.label: unrelated
items.reviewer_rationale: Microvascular circulation uses transport-network terminology but studies different physical phenomena.

items.title: Adaptive rewiring shapes structure and stability in a three-guild herbivore-plant-pollinator network
items.label: unrelated
items.reviewer_rationale: Pollinator and herbivore ecological interaction dynamics should not be treated as transit cascade prior work.

items.title: Decreasing resilience of China's coupled nitrogen–phosphorus cycling network requires urgent action
items.label: unrelated
items.reviewer_rationale: Chemical nutrient cycling and food-system resilience are not validated metro network mechanistic priors.

items.title: Research on the resilience of ecological networks from the perspective of ecological security pattern: a case study of Wuhan metropolitan area
items.label: unrelated
items.reviewer_rationale: Metropolitan ecological landscape networks create a strong urban lexical confounder but not a rail transit model.

items.label: source_self
